The saturation pressure of diethyl ether at 25°C is 150 Torr. If we have a chamber with a volume of 80 liters, what is the maximum number of moles of ether that can be vaporized at 25°C? (R = 8.31 SI)
(Continued: diethyl ether, saturation pressure 150 Torr at 25°C, 80 L chamber.) What will be the vapor pressure of 0.25 moles of ether at 25°C in this same enclosure?
questions.explanation: 0.25 mol < 0.646 mol, so all of it vaporizes: P = nRT/V = 0.25 × 8.31 × 298 / 0.08 ≈ 7 740 Pa ≈ 58 torr.

questions.stem:
One litre of aqueous solution contains:
- 47.4 g of KMnO₄ (M = 158 g/mol)
- 45 ml of H₃PO₄ at 2 mol/L
Electrolytes are completely dissociable. Calculate the osmolarity of the solution.
questions.explanation: KMnO₄: 0.3 mol × 2 ions = 0.6 osm. H₃PO₄: 0.09 mol × 4 ions = 0.36 osm. Total = 0.96 osm/L.

questions.stem: (Continued: 1 L of solution with 47.4 g KMnO₄ (M = 158) and 45 ml of 2 mol/L H₃PO₄, fully dissociated.) Calculate the IONIC STRENGTH of this aqueous solution.
In the P-T diagram of a solution compared to that of its pure solvent:
options: The liquid phase only spreads towards the solid phase.
The solid phase is more extensive.
The liquid phase spreads towards both the solid phase and the gas phase.
The gas phase is more extensive.
The triple point moves towards a higher pressure

questions.stem: The cryoscopic lowering of an aqueous solution of aluminium sulphate Al₂(SO₄)₃ at 0.1 mol/L is equal to −0.64°C. Determine its degree of dissociation α₀. (K꜀ = 1.86)
Given that the diffusion coefficient of myoglobin (M = 17000 g/mol) is D = 1.22×10⁻¹⁰ (SI) at 0°C, what will its value be in (SI) at 37°C? We assume that viscosity does not change with temperature.

Consider the tank below at the initial moment. Solutions (A) 0.15 mol/L glucose and (B) 0.1 mol/L Na₂SO₄ are separated by a movable semipermeable membrane at x = 0. How far and in which direction does this membrane move to achieve equilibrium between (A) and (B)?
questions.explanation: Osmolarities: A = 0.15, B = 0.3 osm/L, so water moves A → B and the membrane moves towards A. With compartments of equal length L: 0.15·L/(L − x) = 0.3·L/(L + x) ⇒ x = L/3 ≈ 16.7 cm (L = 50 cm).

questions.stem: Determine the equivalent capacity of the following circuit. C = 3 µF
questions.explanation: Three branches in parallel: C + C/2 + C/3 = 11C/6 = 11 × 3/6 = 5.5 µF.
